task.name: Policy prose has no provenance marker, so agent-generated rationale can block chartered work as if it were a ratified decision
task.story_text:
## Provenance

- Captured while unblocking #1108 for sprint intake, 2026-08-02.
- Related: #1664 (escalation advisor, shipped v0.12.0). This is plausibly a
  discriminator inside that advisor rather than a new mechanism — the plan
  phase decides.

## The observation

ADR-0006 clause 6 closed one direction of the prose-to-decision loop:
LLM-generated prose may propose, but it never routes. There is no counterpart
on the intake side. Agent-generated prose can block.

#1108 is the worked example. A dev agent implementing a documentation story
wrote a rationale into the routing policy source of truth stating that
reasoning effort was "intentionally NOT score-controlled," plus a matching
paragraph in the operator-facing guide. No operator decided this and no ADR
records it — the axis had simply never been wired, and the documentation pass
codified the absence as doctrine. That rationale then blocked a chartered
story through two independent layers: preflight escalated it as contradicting
"an already-implemented, deliberate architectural decision," and grooming
returned `adr_candidate`. Both deferred to the prose as though it carried
operator authority, because nothing records the difference.

## Why it matters

This inverts the project's mechanical-over-prompts tenet: generated prose
succeeded at constraining the operator, acquiring veto power over chartered
work with no provenance to legitimize it. Any policy assertion an intake check
can cite as a "standing decision" is load-bearing, but ratified policy and
generated policy are stored as the same undifferentiated prose.

Every layer failed closed — #1108 stalled at intake rather than burning budget
against a contradiction — so this is a correctness-of-reasoning issue, not a
safety one.

## Acceptance criteria

- A policy assertion that intake can cite to block or escalate a story carries
  a provenance class: ratified (an ADR clause or a recorded operator decision,
  with the reference) or generated (written by a run). An assertion with no
  recorded provenance is treated as generated — never promoted by default.
- Only ratified assertions carry blocking authority. A story that conflicts
  solely with generated or unmarked rationale is not stopped at intake; the
  conflict is surfaced as a retraction candidate for the assertion instead.
- The inverse degrades safely: an unmarked assertion that is in fact a real
  operator decision is surfaced for ratification when it is first cited, so
  demotion to advisory is visible rather than silent, and the operator can mark
  it ratified with a durable reference. That marking is auditable.
- Any intake refusal that cites a policy assertion names the assertion and its
  provenance class in the refusal, so the operator can see which kind of
  authority stopped the work without reading git history.
- The #1108 shape is a regression case: a story chartered by the milestone,
  contradicting only rationale that a run authored, enters the sprint.

## Example

The #1108 escalation, before and after:

```
Before:  ESCALATE — story contradicts an already-implemented, deliberate
         architectural decision (reasoning effort is intentionally not
         score-controlled).

After:   PROCEED — story conflicts only with generated rationale
         (authored by run <id>, no ratification recorded).
         Flagged as retraction candidate: the assertion "reasoning effort
         is intentionally not score-controlled" is contradicted by
         chartered work and carries no operator decision.
```

## Non-goals

Not a general provenance system for all documentation. Scope is the assertions
intake actually cites when refusing or escalating work. Whether enforcement
lives in the escalation advisor or beside it is a plan-phase decision, not
settled here.

handoff.summary: Added a policy-assertion provenance layer so intake can tell ratified policy from run-authored prose. New stdlib+yaml module src/theforge/policy_provenance.py defines the two provenance classes (ratified/generated, with unmarked resolving to generated), a durable repo-local registry at .forge/policy-assertions.yaml resolved against ForgeConfig.project_root, deterministic citation resolution (id → normalized text → 0.7 token-similarity fallback, with negations excluded from stopwords), and the BLOCKED adjudicator. The preflight prompt now emits blocking_basis and policy_assertions_cited; preflight_flow parses both and adjudicates before the artifact write, resume record, and stop_phase return, so batch preflight caches the adjudicated verdict. Adjudication engages only for policy-founded blockers — declared basis, present citations, or a narrow decision-claim phrase list when a refusal cites nothing — leaving credential/contradiction/dependency blockers exactly as they were. A policy BLOCKED stands only when a cited assertion resolves to a live ratified registry entry, and the refusal text names the assertion, its provenance class, and the ratifying reference; otherwise it downgrades to PROCEED and records retraction candidates plus (for registry-unknown assertions) ratification candidates. All seven provenance fields propagate through preflight.yaml, apply_cached_preflight_state, the resume sidecar, and the audit preflight block, with record schema bumped 32→33 and _migrate_v32_to_v33 backfilling empty values. The escalation advisor parses per-option and report-level policy_assertions as unresolved-generated, the coordinator resolves them against the registry, and render_advisory_for_pending labels each with its class and names generated ones as advisory retraction/ratification candidates. shape_classify no longer routes an AC-bearing story to adr-candidate on a Decision/Trade-offs heading alone; explicit adr labels and ADR-marked titles still win. Documented in docs/guides/policy-provenance.md with the registry format and the operator ratify/retract workflow.

commits.message: feat(intake): classify policy-assertion provenance so generated prose cannot block chartered work

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A policy assertion that intake can cite to block or escalate a story carries a provenance class: ratified (an ADR clause or a recorded operator decision, with the reference) or generated (written by a run). An assertion with no recorded provenance is treated as generated — never promoted by default.
acceptance_criteria.notes: PROVENANCE_RATIFIED/PROVENANCE_GENERATED with no third 'unknown' class; PolicyAssertionRegistry.resolve returns generated for any unmatched citation, and a registry entry marked ratified without a reference is demoted to generated with a recorded error. An agent's claimed_provenance is carried as evidence and never consulted for authority.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Only ratified assertions carry blocking authority. A story that conflicts solely with generated or unmarked rationale is not stopped at intake; the conflict is surfaced as a retraction candidate for the assertion instead.
acceptance_criteria.notes: adjudicate_blocked_verdict upholds BLOCKED only when a cited assertion has carries_blocking_authority; otherwise it downgrades to PROCEED and emits a retraction candidate per assertion. Seam test drives a live run: PREFLIGHT_BLOCKED_ON_POLICY with no registry ends at PROCEED with candidates recorded. Retracted ratified entries also lose authority.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The inverse degrades safely: an unmarked assertion that is in fact a real operator decision is surfaced for ratification when it is first cited, so demotion to advisory is visible rather than silent, and the operator can mark it ratified with a durable reference. That marking is auditable.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Any citation the registry never recorded produces a ratification candidate naming the registry path and the required durable reference, plus a preflight warning; a registry-known generated assertion produces a retraction candidate only, since its provenance is already recorded. Marking is a commit to .forge/policy-assertions.yaml, so it is auditable by construction; the candidates themselves land in preflight.yaml, the resume record, and the run audit.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Any intake refusal that cites a policy assertion names the assertion and its provenance class in the refusal, so the operator can see which kind of authority stopped the work without reading git history.
acceptance_criteria.notes: _handle_preflight_verdict appends _policy_refusal_detail(state) to state.error, rebuilt from the resolved-assertion records so cached and resumed dispatch produce the same text. Seam tests assert the assertion text, the word 'ratified', and the ADR reference all appear in state.error on both the live and the resumed path. The advisor side renders the class per cited assertion in render_advisory_for_pending.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The #1108 shape is a regression case: a story chartered by the milestone, contradicting only rationale that a run authored, enters the sprint.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Covered at both layers that stalled #1108: preflight (test_generated_only_conflict_enters_the_sprint — BLOCKED citing the reasoning-effort rationale with no registry entry becomes PROCEED) and grooming (test_story_with_ac_and_a_decision_heading_is_enhancement_not_adr — the #1108-shaped body with a ## Decision heading and acceptance criteria classifies ENHANCEMENT, while an explicit adr label or ADR title still classifies ADR_CANDIDATE).

deferred_items: Plan Step 5 said to bump the audit record schema 'if new top-level audit fields are added'. The new fields are nested inside the existing preflight block, and the writer-side schema guard does not walk into it (the canonical fixture's preflight block is None), so no bump was forced. I bumped to v33 anyway with _migrate_v32_to_v33 because the block's shape genuinely changed and Step 5 explicitly asked for a migration letting older records read with empty policy-provenance fields. The v33 snapshot fixture is therefore byte-identical to v32.

Reviewer note P2 pointed at shape_check/heuristics.py's implementation_design_dump and implementation_plan_in_body as the other route to ADR_CANDIDATE. Both fire on real code/config dumps inside an AC section rather than on policy prose, and the plan said to keep real implementation-design dumps as ADR candidates, so they are unchanged.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 2 says a BLOCKED verdict may stand only when at least one cited assertion is ratified. That incorrectly applies policy provenance to every blocker. build_preflight_prompt explicitly permits non-policy BLOCKED outcomes such as missing credentials, internally contradictory requirements, and unavailable external dependencies; these legitimately have no policy citation and would be downgraded to PROCEED.
  Suggestion: Gate only BLOCKED verdicts whose blocking basis is a standing policy or architectural assertion. Preserve existing non-policy blockers, preferably through an explicit parsed blocking-basis field, and add regressions for missing credentials and direct specification contradictions.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 2 adds provenance fields to CoordinatorState but omits src/theforge/coordinator/preflight_cache.py and src/theforge/coordinator/resume_persistence.py. Normal sprints run preflight with stop_phase=PREFLIGHT in run_batch_preflight, then apply_cached_preflight_state and call _handle_preflight_verdict. Without copying and restoring the new fields, ratified refusals cannot name their assertion/provenance in state.error, and retraction/ratification candidates disappear from the final run audit. Resume dispatch has the same broken data flow.
  Suggestion: Add preflight_cache.py and resume_persistence.py to Step 2, persist/restore every provenance and candidate field, perform provenance adjudication before the stop_phase return, and test live, cached batch-preflight, and resumed BLOCKED paths.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Carried risk #1 (preflight omits structured citations but still uses policy prose in its BLOCKED reason). The stated mitigation — treat policy/ADR/architectural-decision language in a BLOCKED reason with no structured citations as unmarked-generated and downgrade to PROCEED — is a broad token-match on free prose, the same class of heuristic as _AMBIGUITY_TOKENS (preflight_flow.py:88-92), whose own comment records false-positive trouble. A BLOCKED that merely mentions 'architecture' incidentally while blocking for an unrelated real reason would be silently downgraded. Step 6's test list names the generated-only downgrade but no test for the no-structured-citation prose-fallback path specifically.
  Suggestion: Scope the fallback tokens narrowly (require decision-claim phrasing such as 'deliberate/intentional/already-decided/standing decision', not the bare word 'architecture'), and add an explicit Step 6 case: a BLOCKED whose reason incidentally mentions architecture but does not assert a standing decision must remain BLOCKED. Follow the _AMBIGUITY_TOKENS comment's precedent of documenting why each token is included.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Carried risk #2 (free-form assertion text → registry matching is brittle). The mitigation (prefer explicit ids, normalized text as fallback) is sound, but Step 6 only lists 'registry classification' — no case pins the normalized-fallback behavior, so a near-miss on a genuinely ratified assertion would silently classify it as generated and strip a legitimate block.
  Suggestion: Add a Step 6 case for the text-fallback path: a ratified assertion cited with reworded text still resolves as ratified, and a non-matching citation resolves as generated with a ratification candidate recorded (not silently dropped).
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 3's description ('do not let ordinary enhancement stories become ADR candidates solely because they discuss policy, rationale, decisions, ratification, or retraction') does not match the actual mechanisms. shape_classify._looks_like_adr_candidate fires on heading matches (decision|alternatives considered|trade[- ]?offs?) and _ADR_TITLE_TOKENS, not on prose mentions; shape_check/verdict.py:28-29 maps the implementation_plan_in_body / implementation_design_dump heuristics. A keyword-exclusion implementation would be a no-op against both.
  Suggestion: Direct the narrowing at the real predicates: the decision/trade-offs heading match in shape_classify (e.g. require it in absence of acceptance-criteria/enhancement signal, or let the existing multi-match → UNRESOLVED downgrade handle it), and the design-dump heuristic in shape_check/heuristics.py. Risk #3's mitigation (preserve explicit ADR labels/titles) is retired by keeping the label and _ADR_TITLE_TOKENS branches untouched.
- [P1-impl] [google-gemini-3.5-flash-api] Ensure the registry loader searches for the repo-local policy assertions YAML file relative to the project root directory retrieved from ForgeConfig to support execution from subdirectories.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.

plan_structured.approach: Add a small structured policy-assertion provenance layer and make intake consumers treat generated or unmarked policy prose as advisory evidence, not blocking authority. Keep the routing decision deterministic in Python: LLMs may cite assertions, but coordinator/intake code decides whether a cited assertion can block.

steps.description: Create the policy assertion provenance model and registry loader
steps.details: Add stdlib-only data types and helpers for policy assertion citations, provenance classes `ratified` and `generated`, registry loading from a repo-local durable YAML file, and normalization rules where missing/unmatched provenance is classified as generated. Include support for ratified references, generated run ids, retraction candidates, and ratification candidates without making this a general documentation provenance scanner.

steps.description: Enforce provenance authority at preflight intake
steps.details: Extend `build_preflight_prompt` output to include structured `policy_assertions_cited` whenever a BLOCKED verdict relies on a standing policy/architectural assertion. Parse that field beside existing preflight YAML fields, store it on `CoordinatorState`, and before `_handle_preflight_verdict` allow BLOCKED to stand only when at least one cited assertion resolves as ratified. If the conflict is solely generated or unmarked, downgrade to PROCEED, append a warning, record retraction/ratification candidates, and include those fields in `preflight.yaml` plus `generate_audit_log`. When BLOCKED stands, include the assertion text/id and provenance class in `state.error`.

steps.description: Prevent shape/grooming from promoting policy-ratification stories to ADR candidates by default
steps.details: Keep explicit ADR labels/titles and real implementation-design dumps as ADR candidates, but do not let ordinary enhancement stories with acceptance criteria become ADR candidates solely because they discuss policy, rationale, decisions, ratification, or retraction. The #1108-shaped story should remain runnable/enhancement-shaped unless it itself asks the operator to make a new decision rather than implement chartered behavior.

steps.description: Teach the escalation advisor schema to carry policy citation provenance
steps.details: Add optional policy assertion citation data to advisor reports/options and render provenance class in `render_advisory_for_pending`. Update the advisor prompt so ratified assertions may justify blocking/elevating advice, while generated or unmarked assertions should be surfaced as retraction or ratification candidates rather than treated as established architecture.

steps.description: Add durable ratification guidance and registry/audit compatibility
steps.details: Document the registry format, the rule that unmarked assertions are generated, and the operator workflow for ratifying an assertion with a durable ADR/operator-decision reference. Bump the audit record schema if new top-level audit fields are added, and add the corresponding migration so older records read with empty policy-provenance fields.

Cover registry classification, unmarked-as-generated defaulting, generated-only preflight BLOCKED downgrade to PROCEED, ratified preflight BLOCKED preserving refusal with assertion/provenance text, advisor rendering of provenance, and the #1108 shape entering the sprint as runnable/enhancement-shaped. Update audit schema fixtures only if the schema version changes.

criteria_mapping.criterion: A policy assertion that intake can cite to block or escalate a story carries a provenance class: ratified (an ADR clause or a recorded operator decision, with the reference) or generated (written by a run). An assertion with no recorded provenance is treated as generated — never promoted by default.

Only ratified assertions carry blocking authority. A story that conflicts solely with generated or unmarked rationale is not stopped at intake; the conflict is surfaced as a retraction candidate for the assertion instead.

The inverse degrades safely: an unmarked assertion that is in fact a real operator decision is surfaced for ratification when it is first cited, so demotion to advisory is visible rather than silent, and the operator can mark it ratified with a durable reference. That marking is auditable.

Any intake refusal that cites a policy assertion names the assertion and its provenance class in the refusal, so the operator can see which kind of authority stopped the work without reading git history.
The #1108 shape is a regression case: a story chartered by the milestone, contradicting only rationale that a run authored, enters the sprint.

risks.description: Preflight output may omit structured policy citations while still using policy prose in its BLOCKED reason.
risks.mitigation: Treat policy/ADR/architectural-decision language in a BLOCKED reason with no structured citations as unmarked generated authority, downgrade to PROCEED, and record a ratification candidate.

risks.description: Matching free-form assertion text to registry entries can be brittle.
risks.mitigation: Prefer explicit assertion ids in the prompt/registry and use normalized text matching only as a fallback.

risks.description: ADR-candidate heuristic changes could accidentally admit true design-decision issues.
risks.mitigation: Preserve explicit ADR labels/titles and existing implementation-design dump detection; narrow only the policy-ratification false-positive path.

risks.description: Audit schema changes can break old audit reads.
risks.mitigation: Only bump schema when necessary, add a migration with empty defaults, and update schema fixtures with tests.
